show: In 1999, two authors bet their names on one number: "Dow 36,000."
say: In nineteen ninety-nine, two authors bet their names on one number. Dow thirty-six thousand.

show: Their call: the Dow more than triples, in 3 to 5 years.
say: Their call? The Dow more than triples... in three to five years.

show: So, did it happen? Yes or no. Guess before the end.
say: So, did it happen? Yes or no. Guess before the end.

show: Three years later, the Dow had crashed to about 7,300.
say: Three years later, the Dow had crashed, to about seven thousand three hundred.

show: The book got called "the most spectacularly wrong investing book ever."
say: The book got called the most spectacularly wrong investing book ever.

show: So the answer's no? Not quite.
say: So the answer's no? Not quite.
November second, twenty twenty-one. The Dow closes above thirty-six thousand.

show: Right number. Wrong date. About 17 years late.
say: Right number. Wrong date. About seventeen years late.

show: One of the authors later put it best: "Never associate a date with a number."
say: One of the authors later put it best. Never associate a date with a number.

show: The people who got there didn't time it. They just stayed in.
say: The people who got there didn't time it. They just stayed in.

show: A fund of your own should start at $10, not $10,000.
say: A fund of your own should start at ten dollars, not ten thousand.

show: Who Called It, part 2. Next: "The Death of Equities," 1979.
say: Who Called It, part two. Next: The Death of Equities, nineteen seventy-nine.
